To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 3D genomes of rod photoreception cells and olfactory neurons have distinct structural features that are not found in other types of cells.

we analyzed the 3D chromatin structure of single cells from mouse retina and nose, and revealed that rod photoreceptor and olfactory sensory neuron cells have distinct chromatin organization compared with other cell types.
rod photoreceptors exhibit a genome-wide inversion in the radial distribution of chromatin, while olfactory sensory neurons show an interior bias for the olfactory receptor genes and enhancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the 3D organization of the genome of sensory cells, which are the most important cells in the nervous system.
the structure and function of the 3-dimensional genome, and how the 3-dimensional chromatin architecture is regulated by epigenetic factors and transcription factors.
the structure of the genome in sensory neurons.

the three-dimensional genome structures of single neurons are highly heterogeneous and are likely to contribute to neuronal diversity.

this study demonstrates that single cell 3D genome structure is highly heterogeneous even among a single cell type and that the 3D organization of sensory neurons is unique and different from other cell types, which may contribute to the specific functions of these cells.
this study has revealed the 3D structure of the genome at single cell resolution in two types of mouse sensory neurons.

the 3D organization of sensory neurons are highly specialized for the function of each neuron, which can be revealed by single-cell analysis of the 4D structure.
the genome of sensory neurons is not simply a random collection of genes and regulatory elements, but rather a highly structured and compartmentalized genome.
the 3D organization of sensory neurons is more flexible and dynamic than that of other cell type.

the 3D organization of the genome is not static but varies between cell types and even within cell types.
